extractionMethodology.tooling: pypdf 6.19.0 text-layer extraction of all 420 pages of both PDFs (dump kept outside the repository) + pypdfium2/Pillow renders for visual verification of the Arabic cover, contents, unit dividers and 20 lesson badge headers.
extractionMethodology.english: structure taken from the contents pages (PDF 2-3) AND independently re-derived from every lesson heading in the body; the two sets were compared (identical).
extractionMethodology.arabic: structure taken from the document order: the 13 unit-divider pages define the unit boundaries and the 62 lesson pages (each carrying a 'النقاط الرئيسية' band) define the lessons inside them.
extractionMethodology.arabicBadgeReading: the printed badge is a text run at effective font size 20.0 (the lesson title is 19.0), read per page; where the content stream repeats a run the duplicates are collapsed before parsing.
extractionMethodology.alignmentRule: structural identity only — a lesson is aligned by (chapter/unit number, order inside that chapter/unit). No title-similarity matching was used anywhere.
extractionMethodology.noGuessingRule: no title, translation, code, chapter or lesson was invented, machine-translated or taken from the web or from memory. Every string below is transcribed from the named PDF.
extractionMethodology.normalization: whitespace only (the PDFs separate words with tabs and non-breakable spaces); no wording, casing, punctuation or hyphenation was changed.

openQuestionsForReview.question: How must Arabic titles be supplied for First Secondary?
openQuestionsForReview.resolution: The Arabic PDF is now committed and is authoritative for Arabic wording. Every one of the 13 unit titles and 62 lesson titles is source-backed; no fallback and no translation is used.

openQuestionsForReview.question: Confirm the proposed course slug 'programming-ai-1st-sec' and course name 'Programming & AI' (= 'البرمجة والذكاء الاصطناعي' in Arabic).
openQuestionsForReview.detail: Both remain proposals; the PDFs only print the cover titles.

openQuestionsForReview.question: Which title should the single synthetic Part carry?
openQuestionsForReview.detail: see part.titleCandidates — the brief's suggestion versus the existing Second Secondary convention.

openQuestionsForReview.question: What shape should the Phase L spec / knowledge-model file take?
openQuestionsForReview.detail: The K2 engine consumes a knowledge-model-shaped file. This manifest is structure-only. Decide whether Phase L wraps it into a knowledge-model file for FIRST_SECONDARY (with a FIRST_SECONDARY_SPEC), and whether the Second Secondary file should be renamed/moved to match the new docs/curriculum/<level>/ layout.

openQuestionsForReview.question: Should Phase L also re-point the stale curriculum paths and make Kodgy level-aware?
openQuestionsForReview.detail: 13 executable resolution paths still reference the pre-relocation docs/curriculum/knowledge-model.json, and src/lib/kodgy/response-engine.ts hardcodes the 23 Second Secondary sessions (1-1 … 7-3). 18 of the 62 First Secondary officialCodes collide with those codes. Reported, NOT fixed.

openQuestionsForReview.question: Which lesson code becomes Lesson.officialCode?
openQuestionsForReview.detail: PROPOSED: the English '<chapter>-<lesson>' code, with the Arabic '<lesson>-<unit>' badge preserved as display metadata (arabicPrintedCode). The two editions genuinely print different codes for the same lesson (e.g. English 13-1 = Arabic 1-13), so this must be an explicit decision, not an assumption.

openQuestionsForReview.question: Should the Arabic '<lesson>-<unit>' badge be shown to Arabic-speaking students instead of the platform code?
openQuestionsForReview.detail: The badge is what the printed Arabic textbook shows on every lesson header, so a student holding the Arabic book sees '1-13' where the platform would print '13-1'.

sourceAnomalies.finding: The Arabic lesson badge uses '<lesson>-<unit>', the REVERSE of the English '<chapter>-<lesson>'.
sourceAnomalies.evidence: Visually verified renders: AR page 30 badge '1-3' = English 3-1; AR page 191 badge '1-13' = English 13-1; AR page 217 badge '12-13' = English 13-12. Text-layer runs agree for all 62 badges.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: The same lesson prints a different code in each edition. The manifest keeps both (officialCode + arabicPrintedCode).

sourceAnomalies.finding: The printed badge '1-2' is duplicated: unit 1 lesson 2 and unit 2 lesson 1 both print '1-2'.
sourceAnomalies.evidence: AR PDF page 12 (أخلاقيات المعلومات) and AR PDF page 17 (البيانات الشخصية), confirmed at 5x zoom.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Every other badge follows '<lesson>-<unit>' exactly (61/62). The document order plus the ToC page ranges confirm that page 17 belongs to unit 2 (the unit-2 divider is AR PDF page 16). This is an Arabic-edition printing defect; it is reported here and NOT reconciled.

sourceAnomalies.finding: Only 3 of the 62 Arabic lesson titles are not Arabic script: 11-4 'Queues', 13-2 'HTML, CSS', 13-3 'HTML, JS'.
sourceAnomalies.evidence: AR PDF pages 165, 193, 196 — the badge headings print the Latin words, exactly as the English edition does.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: These are source-faithful, not missing translations; the Arabic contents pages print the same Latin strings.

sourceAnomalies.finding: Printed page 175 does not exist in the English edition (content jumps 174 → 176 at the Chapter 12/13 boundary).
sourceAnomalies.evidence: 202-page file, 198 numbered folios (4-174, 176-202); no duplicate or out-of-order folio. The Arabic edition has no such gap.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: The English page mapping carries an offset from PDF page 175 on; both the PDF page and the printed folio are recorded per lesson.

sourceAnomalies.finding: The 13 unit divider pages carry no printed folio (their page area is a decorative band).
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Unit source references use the PDF page index; lesson references always carry a real printed folio.

sourceAnomalies.finding: The Arabic lesson START page differs from the English lesson start page by 1-5 pages on 24 lessons (never a different order).
sourceAnomalies.evidence: e.g. 1-1 EN p.4 / AR p.8; 13-1 EN p.176 / AR p.178. The arrays are strictly increasing on both sides.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Page provenance must never be used to align the editions; structural order was used instead.

sourceAnomalies.finding: The Arabic edition pluralizes two unit titles: unit 7 'الكمبيوترات' (EN 'Computers') and unit 12 'البرمجة' (EN 'Programming (Python)').
sourceAnomalies.evidence: AR contents page 4/toC rows and the divider pages 96 and 167; English contents page 2.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Titles are stored exactly as printed in each edition; no harmonization was applied.

sourceAnomalies.finding: Chapter 13 headings invert the code position ('About Generative AI13-1'); chapters 1-12 print the code first.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Handled explicitly during extraction; no Chapter 13 lesson could be silently dropped.

sourceAnomalies.finding: Two bracketed lesson titles render with the numeric marker wrapped/placed by RTL bidi rules (6-5/6-6 'العمليات الحسابات العددية [1]', 9-1/9-2 'قواعد البيانات [1]').
sourceAnomalies.evidence: AR PDF pages 74, 76, 125, 129 (heading) versus the same rows on the AR contents pages.
sourceAnomalies.consequence: The stored strings are the logical text-layer order, which agrees with the Arabic contents rows; only the visual placement of the bracketed marker varies.

sourceAnomalies.finding: The two committed files were produced by different tools (EN: Icecream PDF Candy re-export; AR: Adobe InDesign).
sourceAnomalies.consequence: Most plausible explanation for AN-1…AN-4; the Arabic file is the more faithful artwork of the two.

previousManifestComparison.detail: identical 13 chapters / 62 lessons / per-chapter counts and identical English titles and English page provenance; the only substantive change is that the 13 unit titles and 62 lesson titles are now Arabic-sourced instead of null, and the Arabic page provenance plus the AN-1…AN-3 findings are new.
